subject: Weekly leadership signal: decision queue & quickblocks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly leadership signal: decision queue & quickblocks

Good morning team —

Concise weekly signal and ask list ahead of QBR prep. High-level: this week shows steady progress on OKR-Serve latency targets, a customer escalation with Nimbus that's gating a GA milestone, and two decision items that need thumbs-up so we can finalize the QBR narrative.

1) Wins (what to celebrate)
- Serving runtime: P95 tail improved by ~12% after kernel fallback tweak (INF-4287).
- Cost: early batching pilot reduced token cost on internal benchmark by ~9%.
- Customer health: Nimbus PoC completed integration tests; outstanding item below.

2) Risks / quickblocks
- Nimbus escalation: intermittent 503s during peak—CS has a mitigation but they need a config rollback window (see "Escalation").
- QBR narrative: need sign-off on the "Dedicated vs Private" customer case study by EOD Thu to include in slides.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool SLOs will be slightly below target if we hold current autoscale threshold; suggestion in asks.

3) Decision queue (two items) — please reply with APPROVE / REJECT / ASK FOR INFO
A. Approve a temporary autoscale bump for Dedicated pool (increase max instances by 20% for the next 3 weeks) to preserve throughput during the QBR cycle. Impact: ~+7% spend; avoids throttles for two top customers. (Owner: Rishi)
B. Include Nimbus escalation as a featured "customer resolution" slide in QBR (requires customer approval for redacted logs). Need permission to share redacted traces with Nimbus and legal sign-off. (Owner: Marissa)

4) Asks (owners & timing)
- Rishi: decision on autoscale bump by 12:00 PDT tomorrow.
- Marissa: confirm customer permission or alternate wording by EOD Thu.
- Jonas: quick slide approving the lane-level SLO language for QBR (one-liner) — can you take?
- CS (Marissa): provide final support-runbook attachment for postmortem steps — see attached draft.

Attachments: QBR_onepager_v2.pdf (one-pager draft), Sprint_heatmap.xlsx (team heatmap), support-runbook-v1.md (CS draft)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcQBRPrep

I'll consolidate decisions into a short action grid after replies.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks, useful digest. A couple of clarifying Qs before I sign the slide language:
- On the autoscale bump (A): do we have an estimate for expected latency improvement at P95 and the exact dollar delta? If it's the +7% you note, I'm inclined to APPROVE for the short window, but want to call it out in the QBR as a temporary operational lever.
- On Nimbus (B): before featuring their case, we need a single-line approval from the customer and confirmation from Legal that redacted traces are OK. Marissa — can you coordinate? If we can't, propose a redacted anonymized timeline instead.

Also, I'll add a one-liner on 'cost controls during burst' to the QBR deck if Rishi signs off.

Jonas
VP Product
